c.tagline: Alpine capital where a medieval old town meets the ski slopes.

taxi.fareNote: Uber availability is very limited in Innsbruck; most rides are booked by phone or app through local firms such as Taxi 5311. Fares are metered and there is no street-hailing culture.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; 133 reaches police and 144 the ambulance directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The medieval Old Town, a compact maze of arcaded lanes crowned by the famous Golden Roof (Goldenes Dachl), packed with Tyrolean taverns, wine bars, and the Imperial Palace; the must-stay for first-timers who want the sights on their doorstep.

A calm, well-connected district just south of the centre around the main railway station and Wilten Basilica, with fast trains out to the ski resorts; a practical, good-value base for skiers and first-time visitors.
A hillside residential quarter on the sunny northern slopes with panoramic valley views and direct access to Nordkette hiking trails; suits walkers and those wanting a quiet, scenic perch above town.

An elegant, leafy villa quarter of Belle Époque houses near the Hofgarten and the river, one of Innsbruck's most refined and peaceful residential areas; good for a relaxed, upscale stay close to the centre.

A lively local residential neighbourhood just across the Sill river from the centre, with everyday shops, cafes, and parks and easy tram links; an affordable, authentic place to stay away from the tourist crush.

water.note: Alpine tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 5am-11:30pm, with Nightliner buses on Friday and Saturday nights; the Nordkette cable cars and Hungerburgbahn run daytime hours only.
transit.note: The IVB network of trams and buses covers the city and valley, linked to the Nordkette mountain by the Hungerburgbahn funicular and the cable cars up to Hafelekar.
transit.pay: Buy single tickets (about €2.90) or a 24-hour ticket (about €5.90) from the IVB app, ticket machines, or Tabak-Trafik shops, and validate on board; the same tickets cover trams and buses. The Nordkette cable cars and Hungerburgbahn need separate mountain tickets, or ride free with the Innsbruck Card.

bus: Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof bus terminal (ÖBB Postbus / FlixBus)

transit.m: Line F bus to Hauptbahnhof and old town (~20 min, every 15 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or adding about 5-10% for good service is customary; tell the server the total amount when you pay rather than leaving coins on the table.
